text:
Ottawa has points in eight straight (6-0-2), and the run holds up when you look underneath it. The Senators took 59% of the expected goals over those games (expected goals measure the quality of chances) and sit at 54% at five on five for the season, so this is a good team playing well rather than a goalie dragging a mediocre one. Still, Linus Ullmark is the headline: .937 and 10.6 goals saved above expected in 12 games, one year after he finished 13.3 below. Our numbers give Ottawa a 91% playoff chance.

Tim Stützle has made William Eklund's injury (ankle, out until about January) look manageable. He moved onto the line with Dylan Cozens and Fabian Zetterlund and has eight points in a five-game point streak. Nick Cousins is back from the Jakob Chychrun hit that he says was the hardest he has ever taken, and Tyler Boucher, son of former NHL goalie Brian Boucher, has just broken in. The front office may not be finished either: Elliotte Friedman has linked Ottawa to Bryan Rust and Rickard Rakell, as Graeme Nichols of Coming Down the Pipe relayed. Drake Batherson has done his own recruiting, telling Sidney Crosby he "could have my house."

Calgary opens a five-game road trip in a hole. The Flames have a -24 goal difference on -12.7 expected and 46% of the five-on-five expected goals, and our numbers give them a 9% playoff chance. Devin Cooley starts instead of Dustin Wolf, at .905 and 1.6 goals saved above expected. Martin Pospisil is out after the hit that got Chicago's Wyatt Kaiser three games, and Kevin Bahl is out too. Saturday's 4-3 overtime loss to the Blackhawks fit the pattern. Matt Coronato has two points, both goals, in his last ten, where his ice time would usually bring about 7.6, but rookie Jonathan Castagna has given the trip some life with his first two NHL goals.
headline: Senators roll on as Calgary starts a long trip
